The folder-name derivation exists only in the manual "Add project" dialog, never for the startup default. Verdict is clear.

---

## VERDICT: FAIL (2 of 3 requirements MISSED, 1 PARTIAL)

The claim "this is complete" does not hold. Sidebar restructuring did happen, but not the restructuring the user asked for.

### Req 1 — "Keep only Add Project at the top level": **MISSED**

`ui/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:170-175` — the sidebar titlebar renders **both** buttons:
```
170: <IconButton label="Add worktree" ... onClick={() => onCreateWorktree()}>
173: <IconButton label="Add project" ... onClick={onAddProject}>
```
The previous work moved these two buttons *from* the removed `SectionHeader` *into* the titlebar (git diff `Sidebar.tsx` @@ -176,47 +167,16). The global "Add worktree" was never removed — it was relocated and kept. `onCreateWorktree()` is still called with no project argument here, falling back to `activeProject` at `App.tsx:612`.

### Req 2 — "Add Worktree at each project level, right of the project name": **MISSED**

Trace of the per-project row, `Sidebar.tsx:201-249`: the row contains exactly two children — the chevron toggle (`:213-223`) and the project-name button (`:224-248`). There is **no** IconButton, no `onCreateWorktree(project)` call, and no hover-action slot in that row. The `group/project` class added at `:204` is dead: nothing in the file uses a `group-hover/project:` variant.

The only per-project creation affordance is `Sidebar.tsx:263` → `WorktreeList` `onCreate`, and that renders at `WorktreeList.tsx:44-54` **only when the project has zero worktrees**, as a text link "Create the first worktree" nested *below* the project row. For any project with worktrees (the normal case, including `orca-lite`), there is no project-level Add Worktree control at all.

### Req 3 — "Show the repository folder name (orca-lite) instead of `default`": **PARTIAL — not user-visible**

- Backend: `src-tauri/src/lib.rs:127-155` derives `derived_id` from `repo_root.file_name()` and registers it. That part works.
- But `lib.rs:152-154` *also* re-registers the same repo under `"default"`.
- Frontend: `ui/src/App.tsx:52` `const DEFAULT_PROJECT = { workspaceId: DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID, repoRoot: "." }` with `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID = "default"` (`ui/src/lib/tauri.ts:19`). `loadProjects()` (`App.tsx:762-773`) and `loadActiveProjectId()` (`App.tsx:785-790`) both fall back to `"default"`.
- There is **no** IPC command to list registered workspaces (`grep cmd_project_list|list_workspaces` → no matches), so the UI can never learn that `orca-lite` was registered.
- The sidebar label is `project.workspaceId` (`Sidebar.tsx:219`, `:227`, `:232`) — so a fresh user still sees **`default`**.

The Rust change is inert from the user's perspective; the `"default"` fallback registration at `lib.rs:152-154` guarantees the old ID keeps resolving, so nothing changes on screen.

### Test evidence — tests preserve old behavior, do not prove new behavior

- `ui/src/components/Sidebar.test.tsx:81` `"keeps only global actions in the sidebar titlebar"` asserts at `:95` that clicking **Add worktree** in the titlebar fires `onCreateWorktree`. This test *pins the violation of Req 1* as intended behavior.
- `Sidebar.test.tsx:276` iterates `["Hide sidebar", "Add worktree", "Add project"]` — again asserting the global Add worktree exists.
- `Sidebar.test.tsx:245` uses the unscoped `getByRole("button", { name: "Add worktree" })`, which resolves to the titlebar button, not a project-level one.
- No test anywhere queries an Add-worktree control scoped to a project row. `grep` for a per-project button turns up nothing in `Sidebar.test.tsx`.
- `ui/src/App.test.tsx:162-168` adds a mock button `Add worktree to {project.workspaceId}` — but this is a **hand-written mock of Sidebar** (`vi.mock("./components/Sidebar")` at `:129`). It proves only that `App.onCreateWorktree(project)` routes to `setCreateTargetProject`; it proves nothing about the real Sidebar rendering such a button. The real Sidebar does not.
- `App.test.tsx:224, 444-445, 458, 506, …` all pin `workspaceId: "default"`. No test asserts the folder name appears.

Test run: `npx vitest run src/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/App.test.tsx` → 34 passed. Green suite, wrong spec.

### Blocking findings

1. `Sidebar.tsx:170-172` — delete the titlebar Add worktree IconButton (Req 1).
2. `Sidebar.tsx:224-248` — add an Add-worktree IconButton as a sibling **after** the project-name button inside the row div at `:201`, calling `onCreateWorktree(project)`. Note the name button currently has `flex-1`, so it must be restructured for the action to sit right of the name. (Req 2)
3. `App.tsx:52` / `tauri.ts:19` — the startup project must carry the repo folder name.
